# BOOK 1 of 2: The Boy Traders; Or, The Sportsman's Club Among the Boers (Harry Castlemon, Frank Nelson Series)

## Structure
Ch I The Sandwich Islands (p5); II The Gale (24); III The Last of Long Tom (42); IV A Change of Programme (64); V The Two Champions (85); VI The Consul's "Clark" (105); VII More about the Clerk (129); VIII On the Quarter-deck again (149); IX A Yankee Trick (169); X Archie proves Himself a Hero (192); XI An Obstinate Captain (214); XII Buying an Outfit (234); XIII A Surly Boer (253); XIV A Troop of Lions (274); XV "Where's my Horse?" (296); XVI Deserted (317); XVII Conclusion (339).

## Characters
- Frank Nelson: sailing-master/acting captain; cousin of Archie. Frank was "shanghaied" to a whaler (Tycoon) earlier.
- Uncle Dick (Captain Dick Gaylord? referred to as "Uncle Dick"), captain of the schooner Stranger; old sailor, meerschaum pipe, oilcloth suit, speaking-trumpet.
- Walter Gaylord: paymaster, keeps books and key of safe; brother of Eugene.
- Eugene Gaylord: flute player, Henry rifle, brother of Walter.
- Archie Winters: cousin of Frank; lassoes, Maynard rifle, quick-witted, "Yankee" humor.
- Featherweight (Fred Craven), George (George Le Dell), Fred, Perk (Phil Perkins).
- Dick Lewis and Bob Kelly: backwoods trappers; Dick has Indian yells, fast on foot.
- Mr. Baldwin (first mate), Mr. Parker (second mate), Barton (coxswain/bosun), Lucas (old boatswain's mate), Rodgers, Doctor (negro cook), Brown (repentant sailor), Stevens, Freas.
- Waters: giant convict, Englishman, struck Lucas, handspike; Bob (ticket-of-leave man) with revolver.
- Gus Fowler: consul's clerk ("Aw!", drawl), Englishman; plotted seizure.
- Mr. Wilbur: sheep-herder, Uncle Dick's friend (ex-miner), station near Hobart Town.
- Mack (McGregor): Scotch transport-rider/driver; deserted with horse and gun.
- Mynheer Schrader: surly Boer field cornet.
- Kendall: midshipman; gray-headed lieutenant from steamer.
- Blangy, Muriac (engineer), Waters crew.
- Sam: old servant at Gaylord mansion.

## Events (order)
1. Frank and Uncle Dick discuss cyclone; barometer falls; Frank corrects southern-hemisphere cyclone directions.
2. Recap: Tycoon/Captain Barclay; Walter captured by robbers (rescued by Dick Lewis and Bob Kelly); Archie lassoed wild horse, Zack and Silas trappers; box of brass machine not gold.
3. Sandwich Islands (Honolulu, Oahu ride, Hilo). Surf-board challenge; Archie and Eugene back out. Kilauea volcano; trappers' fear; Dick and Bob fearful of whales/quids/lions.
4. Stranger sails to Mangrove Islands; fires thirty-pounder "Long Tom" at natives. Ambush averted.
5. Gale (ch II): crew battens cabin; Stranger dismasted; flying jibboom, topmasts lost.
6. Cyclone (ch III): Mr. Baldwin explains; Frank computes evasion; storm; later Chase's letter in Herald. Schooner driven toward island; Long Tom thrown overboard; natives in canoes repulsed by shrapnel (twenty-pounder).
7. Ch IV: strange ship (Sea Gull) wrecked on reef; eleven men rescued; Waters among them; Frank acting officer of deck; Frank suspects four escaped convicts (Waters, plus three).
8. Ch V: Waters strikes Lucas, seizes handspike; Dick Lewis subdues him with irons applied by master-at-arms; Waters put in brig. Three friends sent to mast; Uncle Dick warns them.
9. Ch VI: Hobart Town, Tasmania; Waters recognized; consul's clerk Fowler visits; police commissioner's boat; convicts taken.
10. Ch VII: Wilbur's sheep station; Archie vs Dick foot race (Dick beats horse; Eugene's horse turns too late); Melbourne trip; Archie's horse stolen by bushrangers; return to Hobart; Fowler chats with Frank about safe money.
11. Ch VIII: Frank locked in cabin; schooner seized by convicts (Waters, Bob, Fowler; three sailors aid). Club left at Wilbur's.
12. Ch IX: Fowler attempts to lure Walter down lane; Bob seizes Archie by mistake; Archie taken aboard; Yankee trick: Frank evades steamer at night.
13. Ch X: Archie shackles sleeping Waters; Frank, Archie, Doctor and sailors recapture schooner; convicts ironed. Steamer under English colors; boat with gray-headed lieutenant and midshipman Kendall; Frank refuses to haul down American flag.
14. Ch XI: Stranger escapes steamer; Club (Uncle Dick) meets Stranger on tug; three foremast hands discharged at Hobart; Stranger sails for Natal.
15. Ch XII: Natal; Uncle Dick buys outfit from English colonel at Grahamstown (wagon, oxen, salted horses, elephant gun); McGregor (Mack) hired as driver; horses drawn by lot (Frank draws number three, vicious horse, heavy rifle; Archie gets thoroughbred).
16. Ch XIII: trek; Boer Mynheer Schrader refuses trade; Frank repairs Griqua gun; Eugene dares night at lion fountain.
17. Ch XIV: Eugene, Archie, Fred spend night in shooting-hole; wild dogs/jackal scare; they fire; Uncle Dick and party arrive; wild dogs, not lions.
18. Ch XV: Mack's odd behavior; Uncle Dick's horse and Archie's horse neigh; Archie retrieves horse from thorn bushes; Kaffirs plan desertion.
19. Ch XVI: Mack deserts on Walter's horse/rifle, sells Uncle Dick's horse and gun in Grahamstown; Kaffirs and Griquas flee; Zulu envoy with two elephant tusks demands gun; Uncle Dick refuses; Dick Lewis's war-dance makes Zulus flee.
20. Ch XVII: Zulu ambush at dry stream; chief shot by Bob; Archie's horse killed; Frank saves Archie; spear through Frank's haversack. Boers trade cattle; homeward voyage; Stranger reaches Bellville. Epilogue: Frank a lawyer; Archie civil engineer, married; Chase and Wilson orange plantation Florida; Fred Craven revenue lieutenant; Jasper Babcock, George Le Dell (Memphis), Phil Perkins (steamers), Walter and Eugene run plantation; Uncle Dick at cabin.

# BOOK 2 of 2: The Odyssey of a Torpedoed Tramp (Maurice Larrouy, 1918, Constable; by "Y")

Epistolary account in letters from narrator (second mate/officer, "old man" addressing a naval officer friend on battleship *Auvergne*, friend's name not given; narrator later reveals fiancée Marguerite of La Rochelle) aboard French cargo steamer *Pamir* (~3,000–5,000 tons; ~35 crew; no wireless, no guns, two lifeboats). Captain **Fourgues** (goatee, slanted eyes, Provençal, from Orange; calls narrator "my boy"/"Sonnie"; cards; rum; rages). Engineers **Muriac** (first, collars for broken shaft) and **Blangy** (officer who left for trawler). **Villiers** (engineer from *Mer-Morte*, later stays). **Fafa** (Fabrice, cocktails steward). Reservists: croupier from Deauville, tram-driver (later navigation pupil), newsvendor, cattle-dealer, movie-man (dynamo), lift-boy, chef of Hotel Romantic. Plantat (*Terre-de-Feu* captain). Flannigan (American, Irish father). Mousseaux (munitions civil engineer). Owner of the *Pamir* (shareholder-minded). Marguerite (fiancée, La Rochelle; wedding at Marseilles, Oct 1916).

## Chronology
- Aug 22, 1914 (Morocco): Pamir leaves New Orleans (cotton, 5,000 bales), shaft broken mid-Atlantic, repaired by Muriac; Irish Channel; destroyer stops them, war declared; Fourgues turns back to France. H---- (Le Havre-like) port: officers and crew taken; reservists assigned; coal tangles; Morocco port (Sunday coal refusal); 1,500 bales left in Morocco.
- Oct 5, 1914 (Mediterranean/K----): coal loaded at K----; German passengers (Boche furniture, piano smashed); owner's deal; post-captain; Lamartine collision (lifeboat/davits damaged).
- Nov 15, 1914 (Cardiff): coal loading at K---- (briquettes vs lump dust); Anti-Paxo; destroyers; Liverpool; cotton to Karl Kristian (Denmark).
- Feb 12, 1915 (Alexandria): Senegal/Cameroon coal voyage; Casablanca cereals; Antivari (Montenegro) night unloading; bora wind; Austrian aviators.
- Apr 8, 1915 (Newcastle): Indian troops (600, three died); Grand Fleet coaling; Fourgues gives narrator command for ten days (ready in eleven).
- Jun 17, 1915 (Malta): shells for battleships (Gibraltar, Mudros); Gallipoli field-guns; wounded; Plantat.
- Sep 15, 1915 (Archangel): Sfax/Cabes; Brest; rifles to Russia; Trondhjem; Flannigan; convoy; Archangel unloading.
- Dec 18, 1915 (Mudros): Newcastle, Southampton; Marseilles/Estaque; aeroplanes; Milo; Army evacuation.
- Jan 30, 1916 (Algiers): meets Blangy; *Mer-Morte* torpedoed; Villiers rescued; German officer explains secret routes; prize accounts.
- Mar 13, 1916 (Salonica): firewood cargo; municipal banquet; Naval Brass Hat.
- Apr 27, 1916 (Bilbao): iron ore; fiancée wife travel story (Syracuse, Malta, Bizerta, Bayard).
- Jul 16, 1916 (Baltimore): La Rochelle visit; Jutland cost estimate by Villiers (~60 million pounds sterling); Mousseaux.
- Sep 23, 1916 (Naples): steel from New York; Flannigan; Brest; damaged hull (hit off Sallys).
- Oct 1916 (Marseilles): narrator marries Marguerite; Fourgues attends, gives wrought-iron lamp; Villiers gives hookah.
- Oct 30 / Nov 2, 1916: narrator's anxiety letters.
- Dec 16, 1916 (Argostoli): torpedo attempt near Matapan; *Worthminster* believed lost; skippers' luncheon; Greek situation.
- Feb 18, 1917 (Norway): narrator's son born (conscript class of 1937; narrator asks friend to be godfather); convoy scattered; Messina/Ajaccio (tow *Sainte Eulalie*); Lisbon; Bilbao; Brest; mine seen in Channel; Liverpool; Bergen; German blockade announced.
- Official statement (end Feb 1917): German wireless reports sinking of the *Pamir*, which is overdue.

Recurring motifs: no wireless, no guns; secret routes; patrols claimed; lifeboats insufficient; Forms and bureaucracy; "Mum's the word"; Fourgues' prediction of submarines; fiancée/wife letters; "Jack Robinson"; "Who lives, learns."
